items.title: Registers
items.text:
• RSP - Stores the stack pointer/address. The first thing on the stack is argc, then after that is the pointer/address to the arguments.
  • RAX - Register used for choosing syscalls. Put the syscall code into it and then call syscall. Also used for returning a value in function calls.
  • RDI - Register used for first argument of a syscall and a function call.

items.title: Register Function Relationship
items.text:
• rax, rcx, rdx, rsi, rdi, r8, r9, r10, r11 - caller-saved, can be touched by called functions, responsibility of caller to preserve values with push/pop
    • RAX, will almost always be clobbered due to it being used for the return value.
  • rbx, rbp, r12, r13, r14, r15 - called-saved, must be untouched by called functions

items.title: Syscalls
items.text:
https://filippo.io/linux-syscall-table/

  • RAX - Used for choosing syscalls.
  • RDI - Used for the first argument of a syscall. Is often the "File Descriptor".
  • RSI - Used for the second argument of a syscall. Is often the pointer to the data for the syscall to use.
  • RDX - Used for the third argument of a syscall. Is often used to store the length used in the syscall.

items.title: Jenkins
items.text:
1. Using choco install caddy
  2. Using caddy put cf onto the server and then run caddy start --config cf
  3. Go to ProgramData\Jenkins\jenkins.xml and change the http port to 8001
  4. Then go to /restart under the Jenkins
  5. To make it run without a terminal window:
    • Start-Process "caddy" -ArgumentList "start" -WindowStyle Hidden
    • caddy reload cf <- At cf location

items.title: Updating Users and Passwords
items.text: In general changing users is done under the software "Computer Management" * Adding users, deleting users, and any user operation can be done here * To monitor logged-in users go to Task Manager and click on "Users" tab * If a user needs to be added to administrator, click on properties and add user to the role "Administrators"

items.text:

items.text:
• Everything in windows is a service
  • Services are OS managed programs
  • Windows Desktop OS and Windows Server can run the same programs, but some server programs dont run on desktop

items.title: What needs to be done first
items.text:
1. Install necessary software (sysinternals) using winget
  2. Make backups of scored and necessary services

items.title: General Threat Hunting
items.text:
1. Check Windows Logs
  2. Check on users, active users, user changes
  3. Check on SSH keys and SSH Config
  4. Check running processes

items.title: Dictionary
items.text:
• Endpoint: Any decive that connects to a network and can send, recieve, or process data.
  • Sysmon: A windows service thats logs system activity to the Windows Event Log
  • SIEM: Security Information and Event Management
  • XDR: Extended Detection and Response
  • Directory Server: Centralized databases that store and manage information about users, devices, and network resources.
    • Active Directory: Windows server version of a directory server
  • EDR: Endpoint and Detection Response
  • Beacon: A type of malware that sends information from a compromised system to the Command and Control Center to signal that the system has been comrpomised

items.title: Recommended Tools
items.text:
• Wazuh | SIEM + Detection Rules
  • LDAP Object Monitor | Active Directory Monitor
  • BlueSpawn | EDR tailored software
  • AtomicRedTeam | Simulate attacks to test endpoint
  • Sysinternals
    • Tcpview - View processes with active network ports (Useful for finding beacons)
    • Procexp - View ALL processes (Use for finding a running malware)
    • Procmon - View processes file operations, thread operations, and regedits (Kind of a large list, may not be very useful)
  • Group Policy Editor
  • Registry Editor - View the registry (Not very useful for search, better to use logs)
  • Task Scheduler - View processes that are scheduled
  • Computer Management - All in one view for managing the server. View users, groups, etc.
  • Server Manager - All in one view for server features. View services and events.
